interface.title: Live Earthquake Statistics (A week of earthquakes, and a record that keeps changing)
interface.stage_of_work: Monitoring and exploratory analysis of a live catalog: judging catalog quality and spotting clustering before deeper study
interface.what_it_is_for: Load the past week of USGS earthquakes in the browser, pick a region, and read off live Gutenberg-Richter b-value with bootstrap range, magnitude of completeness, Omori-Utsu aftershock decay, Poisson-flagged busy hours, depth-vs-magnitude patterns and a running log of catalog revisions.

data.note: Public live USGS GeoJSON summary feeds (past week loaded once, past hour polled every 60 s, past day every 5 min), fetched in-page. 1,734 tectonic events drawn for All events; explosions, quarry blasts, landslides and ice quakes were excluded. Nothing was uploaded.

tree.general: Characterise the recent seismicity of a region and judge how far the catalog can be trusted
tree.specific: Use the past week of USGS events to get b-value, Mc, aftershock decay, busy hours, depth patterns and catalog revisions per region

features.name: Subset selector that re-runs every analysis
features.general: Pick one named subset of a dataset; the map, summary cards and every chart and fit recompute for that subset
features.specific: Region button group (All events, Global M4.5+, California, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico), operable by mouse or keyboard (Enter), refits the map to the region box and re-runs b-value, Mc, Omori, Poisson and depth summaries
steps: press a region button
the map zooms to the region's dashed box
the cards update (24 h count, b, Mc, last hour)
the charts redraw, with 'Too few' where minimum counts are not met
serves_tasks: Restrict the dataset to one geographic subset and have every statistic recomputed
Read the fitted power-law slope and its uncertainty for the chosen subset
Compare the size-distribution slope and completeness across subsets, and recognise when pooled data mix incompatible measurement scales
Flag time bins whose counts are statistically higher than a local baseline

features.name: Frequency-magnitude plot with completeness cut and bootstrap b-value
features.general: Plot a log-scale size distribution (per bin and cumulative), find the completeness threshold, fit a power-law slope above it, report analytic and bootstrap uncertainty, and refuse when the sample is too small
features.specific: Bars per 0.1 M, dots N(≥M), dashed Mc line (MAXC + 0.2), Aki/Utsu ML b-value with Shi-Bolt error, 200-resample seeded bootstrap 95% range, 'mixed scales' warning when magnitude types are pooled; needs 50 events
steps: read the b and Mc cards
hover a bin for count, cumulative and fit values
toggle to the table (M bin, Count, N at or above, Fit N)
expand How this is measured for live values (a, n, bootstrap interval, magnitude-type mix)
serves_tasks: Read the fitted power-law slope and its uncertainty for the chosen subset
Find the detection threshold below which data are incomplete
Compare the size-distribution slope and completeness across subsets, and recognise when pooled data mix incompatible measurement scales
Inspect the numbers and method behind the fit

features.name: Aftershock decay panel (Omori-Utsu, log-log)
features.general: Pick the largest event cluster automatically, plot event rate against time since its start on log-log axes with log-binned counts and a rug of single events, and fit a power-law decay by maximum likelihood when enough events exist
features.specific: Gardner-Knopoff windows choose the busiest M ≥ 4 mainshock; dots are aftershocks per day in 4-per-decade bins; Omori-Utsu p, c fitted with a profile-likelihood p range once there are 30 or more aftershocks
steps: read the mainshock and aftershock count in the footer
hover a rate dot for its bin and count
toggle to the table (From day, To day, Events, Rate, Fit per day)
expand How this is measured for the window size and candidate count
serves_tasks: Find the dominant event sequence and check whether a decay law can be fitted

features.name: Hourly count histogram with Poisson burst flags
features.general: Bin events by hour, test each bin against a rolling-median Poisson baseline, colour significant bins, and show the per-bin p-value on hover or in a table
features.specific: UTC hourly bars over 7 days; lambda = median of the previous 24 h (mean or a 1/24 floor as fallback); flagged when P(X ≥ k) < 0.001; first 24 h untested
steps: scan for orange bars and read the 'N of 144 hours' summary
hover a bar for count, usual rate, tail probability and flag
toggle to the table (Hour, Count, lambda, P(X ≥ k), Flagged)
expand How this is measured for the latest flag and baseline mix
serves_tasks: Flag time bins whose counts are statistically higher than a local baseline

features.name: Depth-vs-magnitude scatter with default-depth diagnostics
features.general: Scatter a depth-like quantity against size, hover points, list the largest events with their depths, and summarise percentiles and suspicious fixed values
features.specific: Depth plotted downward against magnitude; footer gives median and 90% depth; How this is measured counts events at exactly 10 km and above sea level
steps: read the depth percentiles in the footer
hover a dot for magnitude, place, depth and time
toggle to the table (M, Depth km, Place)
expand How this is measured for default-depth counts
serves_tasks: Compare depth against size to spot artefacts such as fixed default depths

features.name: Live epicentre map with hover card and table view
features.general: Map events sized by magnitude and coloured by depth, with recent-event rings, a callout for the latest notable event, hover details, click-through to the source record, and a tabular alternative

screens_never_reached: A fitted Omori-Utsu curve with p, c and the profile-likelihood p range: no region had the 30 aftershocks needed (most was 14, Vanuatu M 6.0)

A populated revision log listing magnitude, location or status changes, id merges or deletions: no catalog changes arrived in the ~3–4 minutes the page was open, and the 5-minute past-day comparison did not come round again in that time
The USGS event pages behind map dots and list links: they are external (one opened in a new tab and was closed without being used)
The other dashboards in the header (Overview, Edit stream, Order book, Space weather): external links, not visited
not_done: Inspect a fitted Omori-Utsu decay (p, c) and its profile-likelihood range: the live data had too few aftershocks in every region, so the panel only showed binned rates
Watch the catalog correct itself: 0 revisions, 0 merges and 0 deletions during the session; only an empty log and its method text were seen

Possible stale table: after switching from All events to California with the b-value and aftershock panels in Table mode, both tables still showed All events rows (M 6.4 bin, fit 17.8) until Chart then Table was pressed (screens/030.webp vs screens/031.webp). It may have been a timing effect; it was not confirmed
Clicking a map dot opened the USGS event page in a new tab (seen only in the browser tab list); no kept screenshot shows that page
No downloads or exports were found in the interface, so none were tested
